newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- OCT 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- OCT 30.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:
KATHIMERINI

--Continuing rumours of taxation of state titles and financial products cause a 500 million dollar forex outflow yesterday, an indication of the negative climate developing regarding economic developments. The Bank of Greece, however, is unconcerned.

--The implementation of a unified wage scale for spring next year rather than a wage increase for 1997 is the government's proposal to civil servants. National Economy and Finance Minister Yannos Papandoniou hopes to put an end to the issue of incomes policy this week.

--Breach between finance ministry and Intrasoft remains over the implementation of the Taxis programme. Yesterday's meeting between Intrasoft president Socrates Kokkalis and Finance Undersecretary George Drys sees both offer conflicting interpretations of contract.
IMERISIA

--The drachma and foreign exchange markets yesterday reacted negatively to the rumours of a pending taxation of state titles and financial products. Finance Undersecretary George Drys states his concern over how these investment products will be taxed and the subsequent effects on the markets.
--New T-bill issue at lower interest rate of 12.30 percent.
--Despite an increase in employer contributions and state subsidies, four of the main social insurance funds remain 200 billion drachmas in the red.
--30 leading retailers get the green light to stay open till 8 p.m. on Saturdays, on a trial basis.
--Olympic Airways, Greece's national carrier, enters the price war with fares slashed by up to 44 percent on local and overseas destinations and new routes.
--Elefsina Shipyards faces new impasse as improved bids for the shipyards have been turned down by the development ministry for not meeting conditions on workers and guarantees.
KERDOS
--The finance ministry's move to tax financial products greeted with reserve by bankers with forex markets seeing outflows of 380 MECU, 20 million dollars and 70 million marks.
--Tight-fisted wage increases for 1997, Finance and National Economy Minister Yannos Papandoniou is expected to tell unionists today.
--Various alternate scenarios are being considered by the finance ministry for reform of the objective tax criteria. Reports say that a complete overhaul of the system is on the cards for 1997.
EXPRESS

--Papandoniou to present final proposals on taxation and spending to the prime minister tomorrow for final decision. Final budget draft to go through party and government bodies before reaching Parliament.
NAFTEMBORIKI
--Continued meetiengs on the budget are being conducted in the shadow of non-existent revenues.
--A flurry of investments is working miracles in the previously depressed border region of Thrace, turning it into one of the most important industrial regions in the country.
--Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
